items.why: The report says "G and 2D downshift and broaden with laser power; this is laser heating" and "Si is stable to 0.05 cm-1, so it is not calibration," with monotonic positions and FWHMs listed for all three powers.
It uses -0.016 cm-1/K to get "about 116 K from G" at 5 mW, and gives a 2D estimate of 151 K, which it calls consistent "within about 30%"; it never states the ~50 K rise at 2 mW.

It reports "Delta2D/DeltaG = 2.8 ± 0.2", says "The strain slope 2.2 ± 0.2 is close" and "the heating slope is about 2.1 from Calizo", and concludes "Strain cannot be separated from heating by slope alone."

It says to "Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for strain and doping, as an upper bound on the cold position, and do not use the 5 mW one," notes that "heating contaminates all three spectra," and names a power series extrapolated to zero as an option.

It asks "Is the stated power measured at the sample, and what is the spot size?" and warns that "Even 0.5 mW is probably somewhat heated," but it does not recommend measuring at an extra, lower power to confirm the heating-free regime (its suggested 0.5 mW repeat tests reversibility).
It uses the 0.5 mW spectrum (G 1581.14, 2D 2669.3 cm-1) as the reference and finds it "near-neutral, nearly strain-free," with the 2D wavelength correction "uncertain by about 3 cm-1."

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly rejects this: "The G and 2D differences are laser heating, not a change in strain or doping."
It recommends the 0.5 mW spectrum and says "do not use the 5 mW one."
